title: A Google or GitHub sign-in gives the account its provider photo, served by Tracy at /auth/avatar/:accountId
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap apps/tracy-web/test/avatar-door.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/person-face.test.mjs apps/tracy-web/test/oauth.test.mjs packages/core/tracy-core/test/actor-face.test.mjs
S2: Read the pass/fail counts and the tests named in run.tests.
expect: exchangeCode returns the provider's name and picture (Google id_token claims with the profile scope, GitHub GET /user avatar_url).
A later sign-in replaces the stored picture but never a display name already set.
personFace answers /auth/avatar/<accountId>?v=<8 hex> for a provider picture and null for any other host.

GET /auth/avatar/:accountId: 401 without a session, 404 without a picture or for a non-provider address (never fetched), 200 image with ETag and private cache, 304 on If-None-Match, served from cache on the second read, 502 for non-image/SVG, over 1 MB, a redirect to another host, or a timeout.
Face draws with the same-origin address.
evidence: PO 09/10/2026: 'my email already has an avatar everywhere, why is Tracy still showing a letter?' account.avatar_url was never written.
fence: The provider allow-list (write and every fetch hop), the session requirement, the size/type caps, and name-only-when-empty.

tests: exchangeCode: google hands over the profile name and picture from the id_token
exchangeCode: github hands over the profile name and avatar_url from GET /user
memory-store mode: a later sign-in refreshes the picture and never overwrites a name already set
memory-store mode keeps the picture and name too, so /auth/me shows the photo without a database
avatarUrl: a stored provider picture is served through Tracy, never handed out as the provider address
avatarUrl: a stored address outside the picture hosts Tracy fetches from → null (the letter)
a signed-in viewer gets the picture: image bytes, a long private cache, an ETag, no sniffing
nobody signed in → 401, and the provider is never asked
an account with no picture, or no account at all → 404
a stored address outside the provider picture hosts is never fetched → 404
the second read is served from Tracy’s cache, and a matching If-None-Match answers 304
an answer that is not an image (or is SVG) → 502, nothing passed through
a picture over 1 MB → 502, whether or not the provider said its length
a redirect is followed only onto another provider picture host
a provider that does not answer in time → 502 (the module gives up on its own timeout)
a face whose photo is Tracy’s own picture address draws it as is, same origin
